config.title: Type forwardRef component

intro.title: Type forwardRef component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom button component that uses forwardRef to allow parent components to directly access its underlying DOM element. You will learn how to type forwardRef components in TypeScript to ensure type safety when passing refs. The main technologies involved are React's forwardRef API and TypeScript generics for defining prop and ref types. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to creating reusable, accessible components with proper ref forwarding.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, forwardRef with TypeScript is essential when you need to access DOM elements directly from parent components while maintaining type safety. This pattern appears frequently in form libraries where parent components need to programmatically focus on input fields, or in complex dashboards where interactive widgets require external control over their internal elements. For example, a data table component might expose its scrollable container via ref so a parent toolbar can implement 'scroll to top' functionality, or a custom modal component might allow parent navigation to focus its close button for accessibility. Developers use typed forwardRef components when building reusable UI libraries, form validation systems, or any component that needs to expose internal DOM nodes to consuming components while preserving full TypeScript IntelliSense and type checking.

objectives: Implement a forwardRef component with proper TypeScript typing
Configure component props to accept a forwarded ref parameter
Initialize and manipulate DOM elements using typed refs
Apply forwardRef to expose internal component methods
Construct a parent component that passes typed refs to child components
Integrate forwardRef with custom event handlers and callbacks
Render components with typed refs in a TypeScript application

steps.title: Import React and forwardRef
steps.instruction: Import React and forwardRef from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and forwardRef from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple items from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs are imported, enabling the creation of forwardRef components.
successCriteria: React and forwardRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and forwardRef from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both React and forwardRef from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Define the component props interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'CustomInputProps' to type the component's props. The interface should have a 'value' property of type 'string' and an 'onChange' property of type '(value: string) => void'.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and forwardRef here

// Define the CustomInputProps interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript interface named 'CustomInputProps' is defined with the required properties and their types.
successCriteria: The interface 'CustomInputProps' is defined with a 'value' property of type 'string' and an 'onChange' property of type '(value: string) => void'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an interface, but check the property names and types. Make sure 'value' is typed as 'string' and 'onChange' as '(value: string) => void'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface is not correctly defined. Ensure you use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'CustomInputProps', and include both properties with the specified types.

steps.title: Create the forwardRef component structure
steps.instruction: Create a forwardRef component named CustomInput that accepts CustomInputProps and a ref parameter. Use the forwardRef function from React.
steps.hint: Call forwardRef and pass it a function with two parameters: props and ref. The function should return null for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A forwardRef component named CustomInput is created with proper typing for props and ref.
successCriteria: CustomInput component is defined using forwardRef, accepts CustomInputProps and a ref parameter, and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using forwardRef and defining a component that accepts props and ref parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you're using forwardRef and the component accepts both props and ref.

steps.title: Type the component's ref parameter
steps.instruction: Inside the forwardRef callback, add a type annotation for the ref parameter. Type it as React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>.
steps.hint: The ref parameter should be typed to match the DOM element you'll eventually return. For an input element, use HTMLInputElement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ref parameter will have proper TypeScript typing, enabling type-safe ref forwarding.
successCriteria: The forwardRef callback's ref parameter is typed as React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the ref type needs to be more specific. Make sure it's typed as React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref parameter is missing the correct type annotation. It should be typed as React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>.

steps.title: Add basic JSX structure to the component
steps.instruction: Inside the forwardRef component, return a div element that contains a label element and an input element. The label should display the props.label value, and the input should have a type attribute set to 'text'.
steps.hint: Remember to use JSX syntax with angle brackets. The label element should wrap the props.label value, and the input element should be self-closing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic form structure with a label and text input.
successCriteria: The forwardRef component returns a div containing a label element that displays props.label and an input element with type='text'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your JSX includes both the label with props.label and an input with type='text' inside a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet return the required JSX structure. Check that you're returning a div with a label and input element.

steps.title: Add props to the JSX element
steps.instruction: In your CustomInput component, add a placeholder attribute to the input element using the label prop from props.
steps.hint: Use the label prop value as the placeholder text for the input element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: using props in JSX attributes
<input type="text" placeholder={props.label} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will have a placeholder attribute that displays the label text.
successCriteria: The input element includes a placeholder attribute set to the value of props.label.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the label prop from props to set the placeholder attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element should have a placeholder attribute that uses the label prop value.

steps.title: Attach the ref to the JSX element
steps.instruction: Pass the ref parameter to the ref attribute of the input element in your component.
steps.hint: Add a ref prop to the input element and set it equal to the ref parameter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: passing a ref to an element
<input ref={ref} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The ref parameter will be attached to the input element, allowing parent components to access the input's DOM node.
successCriteria: The input element has a ref attribute set to the ref parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing the ref parameter to the ref attribute of the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref isn't properly attached to the input element. Check that you've added the ref attribute to the input element and set it to the ref parameter.

steps.title: Export the typed forwardRef component
steps.instruction: Export the CustomInput component using a named export.
steps.hint: Use the 'export' keyword followed by the component name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will be available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The CustomInput component is exported using a named export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're exporting the component using a named export.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is not exported correctly. Use a named export for CustomInput.

steps.title: Create a parent component to use the forwardRef component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ParentComponent that will serve as the parent to demonstrate using the CustomInput forwardRef component.
steps.hint: Define a new component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should return JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new ParentComponent function is defined, ready to contain the CustomInput component in the next step.
successCriteria: ParentComponent is defined as a functional component and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure it's a complete functional component that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parent component wasn't created correctly. Create a functional component named ParentComponent that returns JSX.

steps.title: Use useRef to create a ref and pass it to the component
steps.instruction: Inside the parent component, import useRef from 'react', create a ref using useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null), and pass it to the CustomInput component as a ref prop.
steps.hint: Remember to import useRef, then declare a ref variable inside the parent component using useRef with the appropriate element type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component will have a ref created with useRef and passed to the CustomInput component, completing the forwardRef pattern.
successCriteria: useRef is imported, a ref is created with the correct type (HTMLInputElement), and the ref is passed to the CustomInput component via the ref prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported useRef, created the ref with the correct type, and passed it to CustomInput.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref wasn't properly created or passed. Review how to use useRef with forwardRef components.
